rules.title: The rules

sub.dames: International draughts · 10×10 · 20 pieces each · white starts
sub.dames8: English draughts · 8×8 · 12 pieces each · black starts

p1.x: A man moves one square diagonally, forwards.

p2.x: Jump over an opposing piece, forwards or backwards. Capturing is compulsory.

p3.x: If several captures are possible, you must take the most pieces.

p4.x: Captured pieces are removed at the end of the move, not during it.

p5.x: A man that ends its move on the last row becomes a king. It moves several squares diagonally.

p6.x: Your opponent has no pieces left, or cannot move.

p1.x: A man moves one square diagonally, forwards.

p2.x: A man only captures forwards. Capturing is compulsory.

p3.x: If several captures are possible, you choose which: no majority rule. A multiple capture, once started, goes to the end.

p4.x: A man that reaches the last row becomes a king, and its turn ends there.

p5.x: The king moves one square forwards or backwards, and captures both ways.

p6.x: Your opponent has no pieces left, or cannot move.

p1.x: You need a 6 to bring a token out of its home.

p2.x: A 6 gives you another roll. Three 6s in a row: your turn passes.

p3.x: Landing on an opposing token sends it back home.

p4.x: Stars and start squares protect tokens.

p5.x: You need the exact number to reach the centre.

p6.x: The first to bring home 4 tokens wins. The following places also count in a room.

rules.variantsIntro: One board, several mechanics: each variant is a preset of both.

blocked.b1: Six-armed board with Parchís or Pachisi rules: their tracks are designed for 4.
blocked.b2: Pachisi without teams, or with a number of players other than 4.
blocked.b3: Choosing a die when Pachisi throws cowries, and the reverse.
blocked.b4: Barriers with “leave only on a 6” without the rule “a 6 opens the barrier”: a game could lock up for ever.
blocked.b5: Teams with an odd number of players.

rules.house: You can change leaving the base, captures, safe squares and barriers, within the limits above. A game with house rules is friendly: no rating, no stake, no public league. Every saved setting can be reused (“Auntie Odile's rules”).
